claims.text: A systematically trained machine-learning potential such as an MTP can serve as the thermodynamic-integration reference for multicomponent high-entropy alloys.
Training the potential on ab initio configurations spanning both solid and liquid states will improve reference–target phase-space overlap relative to traditional EAM references.
Improved phase-space overlap will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
The proposed training data should include diverse ab initio configurations from both solid and liquid phases.
The intervention is applicable to equiatomic or near-equiatomic high-entropy alloys.
The applicable temperature range is within a few hundred kelvin of the melting point.
Liquid-like configurations begin to prevail within the stated temperature range.
The machine-learned potential captures many-body interactions and subtle bonding variations across solid and liquid phases.
A comprehensive solid-and-liquid ab initio training set allows the potential to represent a broader configurational space.
Better representation of configurational space improves overlap between the reference and ab initio target phase spaces.
Improved reference–target overlap reduces errors along the thermodynamic-integration path.
The intervention may reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch by approximately 50% relative to standard TOR-TILD EAM references.
The magnitude of mismatch reduction depends on the comprehensiveness of the training set.
TOR-TILD calculations using EAM references on the same alloy systems provide the comparison baseline.
Sparse ab initio training data at extreme temperatures or for highly complex compositions may reduce the effectiveness of the ML potential.
Failure to obtain at least a 20% statistically significant reduction in path mismatch would falsify the hypothesis.
The hypothesis would also be falsified if the ML-reference free energies deviate more from full ab initio benchmarks than the EAM-reference results do.
